purpose: Risankizumab-rzaa is used to treat moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adults whose skin condition has not responded well to other treatments. It is also used to treat psoriatic arthritis and moderate to severe Crohn's disease. This medication helps clear skin, reduce joint pain, and calm inflammation in the digestive tract.
how_it_works: Your immune system sometimes overreacts and produces too much of a protein called IL-23, which causes the inflammation responsible for your symptoms. Risankizumab works like a targeted blocker — it attaches to IL-23 and stops it from sending the signal that triggers that overreaction. By quieting down that specific part of your immune system, it helps reduce redness, scaling, swelling, and other symptoms.
common_side_effects: Upper respiratory infections like the common cold, headache, tiredness, injection site reactions such as redness or swelling, joint pain, and fungal skin infections like ringworm.
warnings: This medication can lower your ability to fight infections, so tell your doctor right away if you have signs of infection such as fever, chills, or persistent cough. Your doctor will test you for tuberculosis (TB) before you start. Do not use live vaccines while on this medication. Let your doctor know if you have a history of recurring infections, liver problems, or inflammatory bowel conditions if being treated for psoriasis.
typical_dosing: For plaque psoriasis, it is given as an injection under the skin — 150 mg at weeks 0, 4, and 16, then every 12 weeks after that. For Crohn's disease, the first doses are given by IV infusion in a clinic, followed by injections under the skin every 8 weeks. Your doctor or nurse will show you how to give the injections at home.
